title: Driving Creek Railway Review
meta_desc: Discover the unique Driving Creek Railway in Coromandel, NZ. Read our honest family review, covering age suitability, value for money.
intro: The Driving Creek Railway is a one-of-a-kind attraction in Coromandel, NZ, featuring a hand-built narrow-gauge railway that winds through a stunning native forest. We took our family to experience it and here's what we thought. With a duration of 50 minutes and suitable for all ages, it's an adventure not to be missed.

sections.heading: What's it Like with Kids?
sections.body:
We visited the Driving Creek Railway with our kids, aged 6 and 9, and they absolutely loved it. The train journey was exciting and the scenery was breathtaking. The kids enjoyed looking out for the pottery kilns and sculptures along the way.

The train ride was smooth, and the commentary provided by the train driver was informative and engaging. Our kids asked plenty of questions, and the driver was happy to answer them.

sections.heading: Value for Money and Insider Tips
sections.body:
We found the Driving Creek Railway to be good value for money, with adult tickets costing $42 and child tickets $15. To save money, consider visiting during the week or during the off-season.

It's also a good idea to book your tickets in advance to avoid missing out, especially during peak season. You can book online or by phone.
list: Book tickets in advance to avoid missing out
Visit during the week or off-season for cheaper tickets

sections.heading: Best Time to Visit and How to Book
sections.body:
The best time to visit the Driving Creek Railway is during the summer months when the weather is warm and sunny. However, if you prefer smaller crowds, consider visiting during the spring or autumn.

To book your tickets, simply visit the Driving Creek Railway website or call them directly. They also offer a gift shop and cafe on site, where you can grab a bite to eat or pick up some souvenirs.
list: Visit during summer for warm weather
Book tickets online or by phone

sections.heading: Downsides for Families
sections.body:
One downside to the Driving Creek Railway is that the train can be quite crowded, especially during peak season. This may be a challenge for families with younger children who may get overwhelmed.

Additionally, the train journey can be a bit bumpy in some areas, so families with very young children may need to take this into consideration.
list: Can be crowded during peak season
Train journey can be bumpy in some areas
